name: Missouri
agency: Missouri Department of Revenue (licensing); Missouri State Highway Patrol (driver examinations)
permitAge: 15 (instruction permit; pass vision, road sign and written tests; a parent, stepparent, guardian or certified trainer signs at the license office) (Driver Guide p. 3, 15)

teen.supervisedHours: 40 hours of driving instruction, including at least 10 hours at night (Driver Guide p. 16)
teen.holdPermit: At least six months (182 days), counted from the day after the permit is issued (Driver Guide p. 16)
teen.nightLimit: Intermediate license: no driving alone 1 a.m. to 5 a.m., except to or from a school activity, job or emergency, unless with a licensed driver 21 or older (Driver Guide p. 16)
teen.passengerLimit: Intermediate license: first 6 months no more than 1 passenger under 19 who is not immediate family; after that no more than 3 (Driver Guide p. 16)
teen.phone: All drivers: may not hold or support a phone, type or read texts, or watch or record video while the vehicle moves; hands-free calls, voice-to-text and GPS allowed. Warnings before 2025-01-01, tickets after (Driver Guide p. 93; RSMo 304.822).

notes: Handbook: Missouri Driver Guide, Missouri Department of Revenue, 'Revised August 2026', downloaded from dor.mo.gov 2026-10-09. Printed page = PDF page minus 2. No official Spanish guide is linked on the DOR guide page.
Written test (Class F): 25 multiple-choice questions, 20 correct (80%) to pass (Driver Guide p. 1, 18; MSHP DE FAQ).

Test languages (MSHP DE FAQ, checked 2026-10-09): Class F written test in English, ASL, Arabic, Bosnian, Chinese, Dari, French, German, Greek, Italian, Japanese, Kinyarwanda, Korean, Marshallese, Pashto, Russian, Spanish, Swahili, Ukrainian and Vietnamese; oral (headphones) in English and Spanish. Not offered in Tagalog or Haitian Creole. Approved third-party interpreters at the applicant's cost. Class M and E tests in English and Spanish only.

Permit supervision under 16: parent, stepparent, grandparent, guardian, qualified instructor, or a person 25+ licensed 3 years with written parent permission; at 16+, any licensed driver 21+ (Driver Guide p. 15).
Permit and intermediate license: driver and all passengers must wear seat belts. Full license at 18 (Driver Guide p. 15-17).

Speed (Driver Guide p. 50): guide table lists rural interstates 75, rural expressways 65, urban interstates 60, lettered roads 55, cities 25, 'unless posted limits direct otherwise'; same page still says interstate maximum is 70 mph. SB 1408 (effective 2026-08-28) allows 75 where MoDOT posts it.

Move over (Driver Guide p. 23; RSMo 304.022): change to a non-adjacent lane if safe on roads with 2+ lanes your way, else slow down. The guide names red / red-and-blue lights only; the statute also covers stationary vehicles with amber or amber-and-white lights. The guide's cross-reference to page 93 is stale.
Headlights required when weather requires wipers (Driver Guide p. 62) and in fog even without wipers (RSMo 307.020(9)).
School bus (Driver Guide p. 23-24): opposite direction on a median-divided highway or a highway with four or more lanes need not stop; following traffic must stop.
Points (Driver Guide p. 73): 4 in 12 months = advisory letter; 8 in 18 months = suspension 30/60/90 days; 12 in 12 months = one-year revocation.
Insurance (Driver Guide p. 79): 25/50/25 liability plus uninsured motorist 25/50.
